# Summary of 2024 Political Manifesto

This manifesto presents a comprehensive policy platform focused on reducing government spending, reforming public services, and restructuring immigration policy.

## Core Policy Areas

### Immigration
The document proposes freezing non-essential immigration, implementing stricter border controls, and establishing rapid deportation processes for illegal migrants and foreign criminals. It suggests an employer tax of 20% on foreign workers to incentivise hiring domestic workers, with exemptions for healthcare workers and small businesses. International student visa rules would be tightened, and a five-year residency requirement would apply before accessing benefits.

### Economic Policy
Personal taxation proposals include raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 annually, reducing stamp duty, abolishing inheritance tax for estates under £2 million, and cutting energy taxes. For businesses, the manifesto proposes raising the corporation tax threshold to £100,000 profit, reducing the main rate to 15% over time, abolishing business rates for high street enterprises, and implementing an online delivery tax on large multinationals.

### Government Spending
The document advocates cutting government waste by 5%, halving foreign aid, reforming Bank of England practices regarding interest payments on reserves, and eliminating retained EU regulations. Claimed potential savings total £91 billion annually.

### Healthcare
NHS reforms include eliminating basic rate income tax for frontline staff, utilising private healthcare capacity, introducing patient vouchers for delayed treatment, and improving operational efficiency. A 20% tax relief on private healthcare is proposed to reduce NHS pressure.

### Energy Policy
The manifesto advocates abandoning net zero commitments, scrapping renewable energy subsidies, and expanding domestic oil, gas, and shale gas production. It supports nuclear energy development through small modular reactors.

### Law and Order
Proposals include recruiting 40,000 additional police officers, implementing zero-tolerance policing, building 10,000 new detention places, and introducing mandatory life sentences for violent repeat offenders.

### Education
The document proposes curriculum changes emphasising national heritage, restricting certain social content in schools, providing tax relief on private education, and scrapping student loan interest.

### Defence
Military spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years, with pay increases for personnel, enhanced veteran support, and domestic defence manufacturing incentives.

### Constitutional Changes
Proposals include leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, reforming the House of Lords, introducing proportional representation via referendum, and restricting postal voting.

## Financial Summary
The manifesto claims £150 billion in annual savings plus £10 billion from additional economic growth, totalling £160 billion. Proposed spending amounts to £141 billion annually, suggesting a net positive fiscal position.
